fieldDescription: Adds an Optimal entry to the autofit goals for every ship on the refit screen. The other goals still use the game's own autofit.

fieldName: Fit for each ship's fleet role
fieldDescription: Fits each ship for the job it's actually good at in a fleet, going off its designation and its numbers (skirmisher frigates, flankers, brawlers, line cruisers, capital anchors, carriers, battle carriers, support, phase and missile boats). Speed compared to other ships its size counts too, so slow frigates and destroyers brawl and very fast cruisers flank. The role decides who it mostly fights, how much firepower it trades for staying alive, speed, how much outrunning its targets keeps it alive, range, point defense and fighters. With it off, every ship gets built as a generic duelist.

fieldName: Civilian ships: fit for the campaign
fieldDescription: Freighters, tankers, liners, salvage and survey ships never fight, so they get no weapons and get campaign hullmods instead (cargo, fuel or berths depending on the ship, then burn speed, sensor profile, sensors, survey and salvage gear, treasure hunting and supply use). Any OP left over goes into vents and capacitors. You need a spaceport to add the hullmods.

fieldName: Civilian ships: build in fleet-wide hullmods
fieldDescription: With Build in s-mods ticked, civilian ships that are staying in the fleet for good (cruisers and capitals like the Atlas and Prometheus, plus salvage rigs) build in the hullmods that help the whole fleet: Treasure Hunt Package, Surveying Equipment, High Resolution Sensors, then burn speed. It works in a single refit and in Optimize fleet, and story points only get spent on Confirm. Built-in ones don't count against the logistics limit, so cargo, fuel or berths still fit.

Optimal looks at the rest of your fleet. Fighter roles you already have covered (fighters, bombers, interceptors, support) and duplicate wings count for less, and with the Auto or Balanced style each ship leans toward the damage the fleet is short on (anti-shield or anti-armor). Basically the fleet as a whole ends up being the all-rounder. Optimize fleet balances each ship against the plan for the others, and a single Optimal fit balances against the fleet as it is now.

The ship you're flying gets fitted to do everything on its own: its role's damage focus goes halfway to even, it fights every ship size, carries its own point defense (at least 1.2x what it needs), has kinetic and armor-cracking damage, and gets a little more survival on capitals. It still keeps its role (a carrier stays a carrier). Optimize fleet plans it first so it gets the best weapons.

secondaryValue: Auto, Balanced, Anti-shield, Anti-armor, Hull killer
fieldDescription: Auto picks for each ship from its slots and role. Balanced covers all three layers, so it breaks shields, strips armor and kills hull. The others put most of the firepower into one layer and keep enough of the rest to finish the job.
Also adds Optimal (Balanced), (Anti-shield), (Anti-armor) and (Hull killer) goals, so you can give each ship a different style.
Auto goes off the ship (speed, armor, slot arcs). Long keeps every gun close to the longest range, and Close favors damage over range.
How long a typical fight lasts. Short fights favor burst damage and missiles, and long ones favor flux-efficient sustained fire.
Counts scripted effects (EMP arcs, shield piercing, damage over time, chain hits) on top of the plain numbers, so rare weapons win when they really are stronger.
Gives rarer weapons (lower drop rate, higher tier, rare blueprints) a bonus on top of how strong they measure. With it off, weapons only win on measured strength (special effects included).

fieldName: Use items you can only get with cheats
fieldDescription: With it off, weapons and LPCs that have no blueprint, that no NPC faction knows and that no ship in any mod carries (console allweapons stuff like Yunru's gyrojets) get left out of fits, Optimize fleet and fleet orders. Omega, Threat and Dweller gear always counts.

When two weapons score about the same, the one the community rates higher for AI ships wins (Grievous69's 0.98a tier lists, so Burst PD over LR PD and HVD over Gauss). It only moves a weapon's value by about 5%% at most. Vanilla weapons only, but other mods can add rows to data/config/jao_weapon_tiers.csv.
How much the rarest weapon gets when Prefer rare weapons is on (0.15 = +15%%), scaled down for less rare ones.
Weapons and fighters you've marked as priority in your faction doctrine win if they score within 1%% of the best other pick for a mount. The game's own refit autofit ignores those marks.

A weapon or LPC from a market has to make the ship this much stronger for every 10,000 credits it costs, compared to what you own (0.01 = 1%% per 10,000 credits). Survival mode prices weapons x10 and LPCs x5. 0 ignores prices. Order fleet weapons never buys from markets, and Optimize fleet only buys with its shop ticks on.
Minimum point defense for the ship's size (1 = enough to stop a typical missile volley, 0 = none needed).
Weapon ids or patterns, separated by commas (stardust_* skips every Stardust Ventures weapon). The Optimal fit never picks them.

With it off, only hullmods that don't make anything about the ship worse get used (no lost range, speed, handling, shield or flux, no higher supply, recovery, deployment, crew or crew salary cost, and no s-mod penalty). With it on, drawbacks get weighed against what they gain in battle (supply, deployment and salary costs aren't scored). Safety Overrides needs this on.

With it off, Shrouded Mantle, Lens and Thunderhead never get added (ones already on a ship stay). With it on, they're scored by the damage they deal and used where they add the most, crew casualties +50%% included. Keep in mind a fleet with a Shrouded hullmod makes the Luddic Path, the Luddic Church and the Knights of Ludd hostile when they see it.

secondaryValue: Never, Frigates and destroyers, When it scores best
fieldDescription: Safety Overrides doubles dissipation, but it cuts range past 450, cuts peak time by two thirds and stops venting. On 0.98.5a it also adds crew losses by peak time used and doubles the ship's crew salary. Frigates and destroyers: only on those, and only when it really scores best (short-range guns). When it scores best: any hull the game allows.
With it off, it never adds hullmods that only help in the campaign (cargo, fuel, sensors, burn).

The most new s-mods one Optimal fit or one Optimize fleet builds into a ship, within the ship's own s-mod limit. Optimal builds s-mods when the Autofit box "Build in s-mods" is ticked, and Optimize fleet uses its own "Build in s-mods" tick.
The most story points one Optimize fleet spends in total, warships first. 0 = no limit, so it spends down to Story points to keep.
An s-mod has to make the ship at least this much stronger to be worth a story point (0.02 = 2%%).

When a clearly better set needs hullmods you don't know yet, or can only fit at a spaceport, it keeps the slots those would take open. The other slots still get the best you have. The log says what's being held.

fieldName: How much better to wait for
fieldDescription: It only waits when the best possible s-mods are at least this much better than the best you have now (0.1 = 10%%).

fieldName: Most days to hold a slot
fieldDescription: After holding s-mod slots this many days for a missing hullmod, a ship builds the best you have into them.
It never spends your story points below this many.

The minimum gain per s-mod gets multiplied by 20 / the ship's deployment points, from 0.5x to 4x, so a 5 DP frigate needs 4x the gain and a 40 DP capital 0.5x. This is so story points mostly go to the bigger ships.
The most s-mods Auto Outfitting builds into a frigate. S-mods already on the ship count.
The most s-mods Auto Outfitting builds into a destroyer. S-mods already on the ship count.

For Optimize fleet with "Change s-mods with credits" ticked: swapping out or removing an s-mod has to make the ship at least this much stronger (0.1 = 10%%). It scales by ship size the same way the minimum gain per s-mod does.

A button on the refit screen (also in LunaLib's refit menu) that plans every ship's Optimal fit with all the weapon and fighter blueprints you know, lists what custom production would have to build, and queues it when you hit Queue all. Turning it off only hides this button.

How much of your credits one fleet order can cost (0.5 = half). The order is always the whole fleet's plan, and whatever doesn't fit the budget (smaller ships last) gets ordered the next time you hit the button.
Random Assortment of Things: a Frontiers settlement with Ordnance Manufacturing takes the biggest ships' items up to its budget, at its prices, paid when ordered. The rest goes to custom production.
Writes each Optimal fit's scores and reasons to starsector.log.

fieldName: Debug: remove all s-mods and refund story points
fieldDescription: Turn it on in a game and save the settings. Every ship in your fleet loses its s-mods, built-in hullmods lose their s-mod bonus, and you get one story point back per s-mod (bonus XP from building them is kept). It runs once each time you turn it on, so turn it off afterwards.
